items.name: Tomato Rice Soup (30 minutes, One Pot)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, plus more to finish
1 to 2 medium carrots, peeled and chopped
1 28-ounce can diced tomatoes with their juices
4 cups low-sodium vegetable broth or chicken stock
steps: Rinse the rice. Put the rice in a bowl and cover it with water. Swirl it with your hand, then drain. Repeat several times until the water runs clear. Drain well and set aside.

Sauté the vegetables. In a large Dutch oven, heat olive oil over medium heat until shimmering. Add the onion, celery, carrots and garlic and season with a big pinch of kosher salt. Cook, stirring regularly, for 3 to 5 minutes, until the vegetables have softened.
Add the spices. Add the oregano, paprika, coriander and a big pinch of black pepper. Toss briefly to coat.
Add the tomatoes and broth. Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juices and the broth. Raise the heat to medium-high and bring to a boil.
Cook the rice. Stir in the rinsed rice. Lower the heat to medium-low, partially cover and simmer, stirring occasionally so the rice doesn't stick, for 15 to 20 minutes, until the rice is tender.

Adjust and serve. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper. If the soup is thicker than you'd like, add water, ¼ cup at a time. Ladle into bowls and finish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, some parsley and a squeeze of lemon, if you like.

items.name: Stuffed Pepper Soup
ingredients: 2 green bell peppers medium dice, (2½ cups) $1.64***
14.5 oz. can diced tomatoes with juices,
steps: Gather and prepare all ingredients.
Add the rice and water to a medium pot with a lid. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat to a simmer. Cover with a lid and cook for 20 minutes. Turn off the heat and set aside.
While the rice is simmering, in a large pot over medium heat, add the vegetable oil. Once hot, add the ground beef and cook for 5 minutes, breaking it up as it cooks.
Using paper towels, blot up excess grease.
Next, add the bell peppers, onions, garlic, salt, and pepper. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables have softened slightly.
Add the canned diced tomatoes with their juices, tomato sauce, beef broth, dried oregano, dried basil, dried parsley, and paprika, stir to combine.
Bring the soup to a simmer. Cook for 15 minutes to thicken and develop flavors.
Fluff the cooked rice with a fork and divide into bowls. Ladle one heaping cup of the stuffed pepper soup on the rice and sprinkle with mozzarella cheese.

items.name: Shrimp Po’ Boys (prawns)
ingredients: 500g/ 1 lb large shrimp/prawns , peeled and deveined – either frozen and thawed (Note 1)
¼ tsp cooking salt / kosher salt , for sprinkling cooked shrimp/prawns
2 – 3 cups canola oil or other plain oil, for cooking
⅓ cup fine cornmeal , or cornflour/cornstarch (Note 2)
⅓ cup plain flour / all-purpose flour
1 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt , + extra for sprinkling
¼ tsp cayenne pepper , optional (for barely-there spiciness)
2 ½ tbsp Dijon or yellow mustard – Creole mustard if you've got it! (Note 3)
1 tbsp wholegrain mustard (ie with the little mustard seeds in it), or more smooth mustard (Note 3)
1 tsp pickle juice (ie juice from a jar of pickles) or white vinegar
4 crusty white rolls , about 20cm / 8" long – or 2 French sticks cut
¼ cup dill pickles , finely sliced on an angle
2 cups (packed) shredded cos lettuce (romaine) or iceberg
Salted table butter , softened, for spreading on rolls
steps: Toss all shrimp in egg, then coat in Cajun coating. Fry 2 – 3 min. Spread warmed rolls with butter, then base with remoulade. Pile in this order: pickles, lettuce, tomato, shrimp, drizzle with remoulade. Enjoy!
Remoulade – Mix the ingredients in a bowl and leave in the fridge for at least 30 minutes to let the flavours meld.

Lightly warm rolls (Note 5) – Preheat oven to 180°C/350°F (160°C fan-forced). Wrap the bread in foil (2 rolls per parcel) and put them in the oven. Turn the oven off. This will warm them through and make them lightly crispy. You can leave them there for up to 45 minutes.
Cajun coating – Mix the ingredients together in a medium bowl.
Pat dry – Pat the shrimp (prawns) dry with paper towels. This helps it stick better. (I just do this in the colander I thawed them in, just sort of moving them around!)
Egg – Whisk the egg in a separate medium bowl. Put all the shrimp into the egg and mix to coat.

Coat shrimp/prawns – Pick up a shrimp with your hand and let the excess egg drip off, then place into the Cajun flour bowl. Do as many shrimp as you can do so they are in a single layer on the flour mixture. Pick up the bowl and toss to coat the shrimp in the flour.
Grab a few shrimp in your hand and lightly squeeze to adhere the coating well, shake off excess flour (using your fingers as a colander!), then put on a plate. Repeat with all remaining shrimp.

Fry – Heat 2cm / 0.8" of oil in a heavy based skillet or large pot over medium high heat to 180°C/350°F. Fry half the shrimp for 2 – 3 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon onto a paper towel lined plate to drain. Repeat with remaining shrimp. Sprinkle with ¼ teaspoon salt.

Stuff – To assemble the sandwich, split a roll but don't cut all the way through. Spread the base with butter then 1 tablespoon of remoulade. Layer with pickles then tomato and shredded lettuce. Stuff with as many shrimp as you can, then drizzle with a generous amount of remoulade. Devour immediately!

items.name: Sweet Potato Casserole
ingredients: 3 lb. sweet potatoes (about 3 large), peeled, cut into 1" pieces
½ cup (packed; 100 g) dark brown sugar, divided
½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled, divided
3½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or 2¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, divided
steps: Preheat oven to 350°. Place 3 lb. sweet potatoes (about 3 large), peeled, cut into 1" pieces, in a 13x9" baking dish or on a foil-lined baking sheet. Cover with foil and bake until tender, 50–60 minutes. Do Ahead: Sweet potatoes can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool; cover and chill.

Whisk 2 large eggs, room temperature, ¼ cup half-and-half, ¼ cup (packed; 50 g) dark brown sugar, ¼ cup (½ stick) unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled, and 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a small bowl to combine.

Transfer half of sweet potatoes to a food processor, add half of egg mixture, and process until smooth, about 2 minutes. Transfer purée to a large mixing bowl. Repeat with remaining sweet potatoes and egg mixture. Scrape all of purée into baking dish (no need to clean).

Combine 2 cups cornflakes, 1 tsp. ground cinnamon, remaining ¼ cup (packed; 50 g) dark brown sugar, remaining ¼ cup (½ stick) unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled, and remaining 1½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large resealable plastic bag, seal, and shake to coat cereal.

Arrange cornflake mixture and marshmallows over top of purée in alternating diagonal stripes. Bake casserole until marshmallows are golden brown, 25–30 minutes. Editor’s note: This sweet potato casserole was first published in 2023; it has been updated for style. Head this way for more of our best recipes for sweet potatoes →

items.name: Apple Juice Bread
ingredients: 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt
steps: Mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

Set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.

) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold.
Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

Transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

Place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center.

Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.

) Working very quickly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

Bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing. Do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.

items.name: Pear Tart
ingredients: 6 tablespoons unsalted butter sliced into 6 even pieces
1 ½ teaspoons ground cinnamon plus additional for serving
½ to 1 teaspoon flaky sea salt or kosher salt
3 to 5 firm Anjou or Bosc pears sliced ⅛ inch thick -I do not recommend Bartlett as they don’t hold their shape well in baking
1 sheet frozen puff pastry thawed according to package directions
1 large egg beaten with 1 teaspoon water to create an egg wash
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Drizzle the honey onto the parchment in 6 evenly spaced squiggly puddles so that you have 2 rows of 3. I draw a straight line that is about 2 inches long, then snake the honey back and forth over the line in an “S” shape (see video). Place a pat of butter in the center of each.
Sprinkle each pat of butter with a pinch each of brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt.

Fan the pear slices over the butter in a line so that you create 3 long columns side by side. Start with the right or left side, fanning the pears over 3 pats of butter. Tuck the slices snugly against each other so no parchment peeks through (they'll rise up and over the butter pats). For the side columns, face cut edges towards or away from you.

Once you’ve finished the first column, complete the middle column, nestling the pears between the 2 columns of butter so they are directly on the parchment. For this column, face the pears left and/or right.
Complete the final column, arranging the pears over the remaining pats. They should form a rectangle that’s about 8×10 inches.

Unfold the puff pastry on a lightly floured work surface and roll it into a rectangle that’s about 2 inches larger than the pears (approximately 10×12 inches). Cover the pears with the pastry like a blanket. Use the tines of a fork to crimp all the way around the edges of the pastry to create a border.
Brush the pastry lightly and evenly with the egg wash. Dab up any pools of extra egg wash with a paper towel.
Bake the pear tart for 25 to 30 minutes on the center rack, until the pastry is deeply golden and puffed.

Let rest for 5 to 10 minutes. Set a large cutting board over the pan and, in a single, confident motion, flip it over. Lift away the pan and peel off the parchment. Dust with cinnamon. Slice into squares of desired size.

items.name: Sweet Potato Quinoa Bowl
ingredients: 1 large sweet potato (cut lengthwise (11 to 12 ounces total))
1 ½ cups cooked quinoa (frozen or shelf stable works fine)
¾ cup unsweetened coconut milk beverage
1 ½ tablespoon brown sugar (I used Wholesome Yum sugar-free)
4 grams coconut milk powder (I use KOS, 2 scoops)
¼ teaspoon ground cinnamon (plus more for topping)
2 tablespoons coconut whipped cream (or whipped cream of choice)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Lightly spray the cut side of the sweet potato with oil and place cut-side down on a sheet pan lined with parchment.
Roast until very tender and caramelized, about 25 to 35 minutes, depending on the size.
Scoop out the sweet potato flesh and mash it in a medium bowl with coconut milk, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, ginger and salt until creamy. Keep warm.
Meanwhile, add the cooked quinoa, coconut milk, coconut milk powder, brown sugar, cinnamon and salt to a small saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until hot and creamy.
Spoon the warm coconut quinoa into two bowls. Top with the warm sweet potato mixture, fresh blueberries, pecans and top with whipped cream and a dusting of cinnamon.

items.name: Skillet Pierogi with Mushrooms
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 pound frozen potato pierogi, no need to defrost
A fistful of chopped herbs, such as chives and dill
steps: Start with the vegetables: Heat a large, deep skillet (ideally one with a lid) over medium-high heat. Add butter and 1 tablespoon of the olive oil. Once both are hot, add onion, season with salt and pepper, and cook until softened and turning golden at the edges, about 5 minutes.

Add garlic and cook for one minute more. Add mushrooms, season with additional salt and pepper, and let cook in skillet, unstirred, until brown underneath, about 4-5 minutes. Once browned, cook, stirring, until any liquid released is cooked off.
Transfer onions and mushrooms to a plate, bowl, or back to the cutting board to rest.

Brown and cook the pierogi: Add remaining tablespoon of oil to the pan, warm it, and add frozen pierogi in a single layer. Cook until browned underneath, about 5 minutes, and turn each over. Add water (be careful, it’s going to erupt in steam) and quickly cover the pan, reducing the heat to medium.

Cook/steam the pierogi for 5 to 8 minutes, checking once a few minutes in to make sure all of the liquid hasn’t steamed off, and adding a few tablespoons more if so. Taste a pierogi to make sure it’s hot and cooked through and once it is, you’re done.

To finish: Return the mushrooms and onions to the skillet and stir to rewarm them. Remove from the heat and drizzle white vinegar over the pan, followed by dollops of sour cream and your chopped herbs. Bring to the table and dive in.

items.name: Smothered Pork Chops
ingredients: ½ tsp black pepper freshly cracked, (divided)
steps: Gather and prepare all ingredients.
Heat the oil in a medium cast-iron over medium-high heat. Pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and season evenly with ¼ tsp salt, ¼ tsp pepper, and paprika.
Sprinkle the flour on a plate and dredge the pork chops in the flour. Reserve the remaining flour to make the roux.

Once the pan is hot, gently place the pork in the cast-iron. Let the pork cook undisturbed for 3-4 minutes on each side until a golden-brown crust forms. Remove the cooked pork from the pan and set them aside on a plate while you make the sauce.
Turn the heat to medium, and add the onions, stirring occasionally. Cook until they start to brown, for about 5 minutes.
Melt the butter and add the garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Sprinkle in 2 Tbsp of the reserved flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken broth, heavy cream, thyme, and remaining salt and pepper. Cook until it thickens, for about 5 minutes.
Return the pork and any juices to the skillet to warm it through.

items.name: Soothing Rice Porridge
ingredients: 1 cup short-grain rice, washed, soaked if desired
6 cups low-sodium broth (any kind) or water
Toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, and/or thinly sliced scallions (for serving)
steps: Combine 1 cup short-grain rice, washed, soaked if desired, ¼ cup dried wakame (seaweed), 1 Tbsp. dried red shiso, and 6 cups low-sodium broth (any kind) or water in a large donabe, medium Dutch oven, or other heavy pot. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat (you’ll hear bubbling).
Uncover and stir, making sure nothing is stuck to bottom of pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Continue to cook porridge 30 minutes more (resist the urge to peek).

Remove pot from heat and let porridge sit (still covered) 10 minutes. Uncover and stir. Rice grains should be cooked through, broken open, and creamy, but porridge should still be fairly loose. Season porridge with fine sea salt.
Ladle porridge into bowls and serve, topped with toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, and/or thinly sliced scallions.

items.name: Blue Cheese Dressing
ingredients: 120g / 3 oz Roquefort, or other creamy blue cheese – about 1 lightly packed cup when crumbled (Note 1)
½ cup buttermilk , plus more as needed (Note 3 for substitute)
2 tsp apple cider vinegar , or lemon juice
¼ tsp cooking salt / kosher salt
steps: Mash – Put the blue cheese in a bowl and mash with a fork until it's crumbly (blue cheese is soft so it's easy).

Whisk – Add the remaining ingredients and whisk vigorously for about 15 seconds so the blue cheese blends in. There will be some little lumps – this is normal. Desirable! Lovely little pops of blue cheese (for completely smooth, see Note 4 ).
Thickness – This dressing is pretty thick, ideal for dipping, and clings well to leafy greens. To loosen, add a little bit more buttermilk.

items.name: 29 Best Pumpkin Desserts to Bake This Fall
Easy Homemade Cranberry Sauce
ingredients: 1–2 Tbsp. Grand Marnier, Cointreau, or other orange liqueur (optional)
steps: Cook 1 (12-oz.) bag fresh or frozen cranberries, ¾ cup granulated sugar, 1–2 Tbsp. Grand Marnier, Cointreau, or other orange liqueur (if using), 1 Tbsp.

finely grated orange zest, a pinch of kosher salt, and 1 cup water in a medium saucepan over medium heat, stirring often to prevent scorching, until cranberries burst and sauce becomes jammy and coats a spoon, about 10 minutes.Let cool before serving.

Do ahead: Cranberry sauce can be made 5 days ahead. Transfer to an airtight container; cover and refrigerate until well chilled. Editor’s note: This recipe originally appeared in Priya Krishna’s story “Cranberry Sauce Is the Last Thing You Should Stress About on Thanksgiving.
” Find more of our favorite Thanksgiving side dishes here →

items.name: Turkey and Black Bean Enchiladas
ingredients: 8 6-inch whole wheat flour tortillas (I use low carb (La Tortilla Factory))
1-2 tbsp chipotle chiles in adobo sauce
kosher salt ( and fresh pepper to taste)
steps: In a medium saucepan, spray cooking spray and sauté garlic.
Add chiles, chili powder, cumin, chicken broth, tomato sauce, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5-10 minutes. Set aside until ready to use.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat, spray with oil and brown the turkey, season with salt and cook, breaking it up with a wooden spoon about 5 minutes.
When the turkey is browned, add onion, garlic, black beans, cilantro, green chiles, diced tomatoes, cumin and chili powder.
Mix well and simmer covered on low heat, 20 minutes, to let the flavors meld.
Remove lid and simmer on medium-low an additional 5 minutes, to reduce the liquid.
Preheat oven to 400F. Spray a 13 x 9-inch glass baking dish with non-stick spray.
Put ½ cup turkey mixture into each tortilla and roll it.
Place on baking dish seam side down. Top with enchilada sauce and cheese.
Cover with foil and bake in the oven on the middle rack for 20-25 minutes.
Top with your favorite toppings.

items.name: Sweet Potato Souffle
ingredients: 5 large sweet potatoes (about 7 cups once mashed)
6 tablespoons unsalted butter melted or at room temperature
½ teaspoon ground cinnamon increase to 1 teaspoon if you LOVE cinnamon
¼ cup flaked coconut optional (I used unsweetened; sweetened will work too)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil or parchment paper. With a fork, poke holes in the outsides of the sweet potatoes. Bake for 40 to 60 minutes (timing will depend upon the size of your sweet potatoes), until very tender when pierced with a fork. Set aside to cool.
Reduce the oven temperature to 350°F. Coat a 9×13 casserole dish or similar 2 ½ quart casserole dish with nonstick spray.

Once the sweet potatoes are cool enough to handle, remove the peels. Scoop out the sweet potato flesh and place it in a large mixing bowl or the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment. (You can also use an electric hand mixer.)
Add the butter, eggs, sugar, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, salt, and milk.
Beat until smoothly combined.
Scoop into the prepared baking dish.

Next, prepare the topping. In a medium mixing bowl, melt the butter. Sprinkle the chopped pecans, coconut, brown sugar, flour, and salt over the top. Stir until evenly moistened and combined. Scatter the streusel topping over the sweet potatoes in an even layer.
Bake the sweet potato souffle until the topping is lightly browned and your kitchen smells amazing, about 40 minutes. Let rest 5 minutes, then enjoy warm.

items.name: Pork Stew
ingredients: 2 ½ pounds boneless pork shoulder also sold as pork butt, cut into 1 ½-inch chunks
2 tablespoons canola oil or grapeseed or another neutral cooking oil
1 ½ cups dry hard cider or dry white wine such as Sauvignon Blanc (see notes to use non-alcoholic apple cider)
3 medium carrots peeled and ½-inch diced
2 russet potatoes peeled and ½-inch diced
1 tablespoon Dijon mustard plus more to taste
Chopped fresh parsley or sage for serving
steps: Place the pork in a large bowl and toss with the flour, salt, and pepper until coated on all sides.

Heat a Dutch oven or similar large soup pot over medium. Once hot, add 1 tablespoon of the oil and let warm about 30 seconds. Add half of the pork in a single layer (the pieces should barely touch). Let it cook undisturbed for 3 minutes until lightly browned on the first side, then flip and brown on the other side. Remove to a plate. Repeat with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and remaining pork.
While the pork sears, chop the onion into ½-inch pieces.

Once all of the pork is browned and removed to a plate, reduce the heat to medium-low. Add the onion and cook, stirring periodically and scraping the bottom, until softened and browned at the edges, about 10 minutes.
While the onion browns, peel the apple and grate on a coarse box grater. Smash the garlic, then peel and roughly chop.
Once the onions are browned, stir in the garlic and apple and cook just until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the hard cider and apple cider vinegar and bring to a simmer. With a rubber spatula or wooden spoon, scrape up any bits stuck to the bottom of the pot. Let simmer 2 minutes to reduce slightly.

Return the pork and any juices that have collected on the plate to the pot. Stir in the chicken broth, Worcestershire, sage, bay leaves, and cinnamon stick. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a simmer over low. Cover, leaving the lid just slightly ajar, and simmer for 90 minutes. Lift the lid and stir periodically to ensure nothing is sticking. The liquid will noticeably reduce.

While the pork simmers, peel the carrots, parsnips, and potatoes. Cut each into ½-inch cubes. Once the pork has been simmering 90 minutes, stir them in. Cover the pot partway and simmer 45 minutes to 1 hour more, until the vegetables are tender.
Stir from time to time to prevent sticking, and if at any point the stew is thicker than you would like, add water as needed (I added about a cup but it's also VERY dry where I live).

Fish out and discard the bay leaves and cinnamon stick. Stir in the Dijon and let cook 2 minutes. With a potato masher, lightly mash the stew a bit. This will break up a few of the potatoes to slightly thicken the broth and also give you smaller bits of pork mixed in with the larger. Taste and adjust the salt, pepper, and mustard as desired. Serve hot with parsley or sage sprinkled over the top.

items.name: Chili Crisp Yogurt Chicken
ingredients: 1¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, divided, plus more
1 cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt, divided
¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. well-stirred chili crisp
3 cups cooked jasmine or short-grain rice
½ medium head of green cabbage (about 1 lb.), very thinly sliced
steps: Preheat oven to 425°. Season 6–8 skinless, boneless chicken thighs (1½–2 lb.) with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.
Whisk together ¾ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt and ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. well-stirred chili crisp in a large bowl. Add chicken thighs and toss to coat.

Arrange chicken on a rimmed baking sheet and top with any yogurt mixture left in bowl. Bake chicken until deeply browned and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a thigh registers 165°, 25–30 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate.
Spread 3 cups cooked jasmine or short-grain rice over baking sheet with chicken juices and bake until most of the juices have been absorbed and rice is starting to crisp in spots, 12–15 minutes.

Meanwhile, whisk together 1 Tbsp. finely grated lime zest, ¼ cup fresh lime juice, ½ tsp. sugar, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, and remaining ¼ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt in a small bowl.

Combine ½ medium head of green cabbage (about 1 lb.), very thinly sliced, and a big pinch of Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt in a large bowl. Using your hands, scrunch cabbage gently to soften. Add 1 small red onion, thinly sliced, 1 cup finely chopped cilantro, and yogurt dressing and toss to combine. Taste cabbage slaw and season with more salt if needed.
Slice chicken as desired and serve with crisped rice and cabbage slaw.

items.name: Make-Ahead Mashed Potatoes
ingredients: 4 lb. medium Yukon Gold potatoes, scrubbed
1¼ cups (2½ sticks) unsalted butter, cut into pieces
A potato ricer or food mill fitted with fine disk
steps: Place 4 lb. medium Yukon Gold potatoes, scrubbed, in a large pot and pour in cold water to cover by 1". Add a large handful of kosher salt (water should taste briny, like the ocean) and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until potatoes are very tender but not crumbly, 30–40 minutes. Drain and return potatoes to warm pot to dry (off heat).
Meanwhile, heat ⅔ cup heavy cream and ⅔ cup whole milk in a small saucepan over medium until just about to simmer. Reduce heat to low and keep warm until ready to add to potatoes.

Pass hot potatoes and 1¼ cups (2½ sticks) unsalted butter, cut into pieces, through ricer into a large bowl (this will help combine them quickly; most of the skins should stay behind, but pick out any small pieces that get through if you want); season generously with salt. Mix with a potato masher until butter is melted and combined.

Gradually add half of the warm cream mixture to mashed potatoes, folding with a spatula until combined, followed by ½ cup sour cream. Gradually add remaining cream mixture until you reach your desired consistency (the potatoes will thicken slightly as they sit). Taste and season with salt and freshly ground black pepper as desired.
Transfer mashed potatoes to a baking dish or other shallow container, let them cool until the potatoes stop steaming, then cover and chill up to 2 days.

To serve, transfer refrigerated potatoes to a small pot and add ⅓ cup heavy cream and ⅓ cup whole milk; reheat over medium-low, stirring often (but gently) to prevent scorching. Editor’s note: This recipe for make-ahead mashed potatoes was first published in our November 2018 issue; it has been updated for style. Head this way for more great make-ahead Thanksgiving recipes →

items.name: Rasta Pasta
steps: Gather all ingredients.
Dice onion, slice bell peppers, and mince garlic.
Slice each chicken breast horizontally in half to create four thin cutlets. Season both sides with about 1 tablespoon of the jerk seasoning.

Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven or deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook for 3-4 minutes per side, or until browned and cooked through with the temperature reading at least 165°F. Transfer the chicken to a plate to rest.

Add the onion and bell peppers to the same pot. Cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables begin to soften and the browned bits from the chicken have loosened from the bottom of the pot.
Add the garlic and remaining ½ tablespoon jerk seasoning. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.

Add the penne and chicken broth. Stir to combine and bring to a simmer. Cook uncovered for 8-10 minutes, stirring frequently (see notes) so the pasta doesn't stick, until the pasta is nearly tender and most of the broth has been absorbed.
Stir in the half-and-half and continue cooking for 3-4 minutes, stirring frequently, until the pasta is tender and the sauce is creamy.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the Parmesan. If the sauce is thicker than you’d like, add a splash of water or broth.
Slice the chicken into strips, cutting against the grain to keep the chicken juicy. (see notes)
Add sliced chicken onto pasta and finish with sliced green onion and a squeeze of fresh lime if desired. Enjoy.

items.name: Crockpot Chicken with Apples
ingredients: 8 ounces peeled pearl onions (frozen is fine)
2 gala apples (or any sweet apples, peeled and sliced (about 2 cups of slices))
steps: Season the chicken with salt. Heat a large skillet over medium heat and spray with oil, add the garlic and brown 30 to 60 seconds. Transfer to the slow cooker.
Add the chicken to the skillet over medium-high heat and brown 1 to 2 minutes on each side. Transfer to the slow cooker.
Add the pearl onions and pour the apple cider over the chicken, place the herbs on top of the chicken and cover. Cook until the chicken is fork tender on low for 7 to 8 hours (or on high for 5 to 6).

When there’s 2 hours left of cooking, remove the herbs from the top of the chicken and transfer ¼ cup of the cooking liquid to a small bowl and stir in cornstarch. Mix the dijon into the cornstarch slurry and return it to the slow cooker, gently stirring to mix.
Add the apples on top of the chicken, add more fresh thyme and rosemary and cover to finish cooking. The chicken should be tender, fall apart easily and slightly golden in color when it’s ready.

items.name: Creamy Chickpea Skillet with Spinach and Feta
ingredients: ½ cup whole-milk Greek yogurt, at room temperature
steps: Soften the onion. Set a large skillet over medium heat and add the extra virgin olive oil. Once it shimmers, add the onion and a big pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until soft and just turning golden, 4 to 5 minutes.

Bloom the garlic and spices. Add the garlic, oregano (rub it between your palms as it goes in), coriander, and paprika. Stir just until fragrant, 30 seconds to 1 minute. Don't let the garlic brown or it will taste bitter.

Toast the chickpeas. Add the chickpeas and a big pinch of salt and pepper. Toss to coat in the spiced oil and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until some of the chickpeas begin to pop and pick up a little color.
Simmer. Pour in the broth and bring to a boil. Turn the heat to low and simmer until the broth is slightly reduced, 5 minutes.
Wilt the spinach. Stir in the spinach and half of the lemon zest and cook just until the spinach wilts, 1 to 2 minutes.

Temper the yogurt. Add the yogurt to a medium bowl. Ladle about ½ cup of the hot broth from the skillet into the yogurt, a few spoonfuls at a time, whisking constantly until smooth and loose. Turn off the heat, then stir the tempered yogurt into the chickpeas until the sauce turns creamy.

Finish and serve. Stir in the lemon juice, feta, and parsley. Taste and adjust with salt, pepper, or more lemon. Finish with the remaining lemon zest and a generous drizzle of extra virgin olive oil. Serve warm with crusty bread.

items.name: Broiled Salmon Teriyaki
ingredients: ⅓ cup (packed; 67 g) dark brown sugar
1 1½–2-lb. skinless or skin-on center-cut salmon fillet
Thinly sliced scallions and/or toasted sesame seeds (for serving; optional)
steps: Bring ⅓ cup (packed; 67 g) dark brown sugar, ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 Tbsp. unseasoned rice vinegar, and 2 tsp. toasted sesame oil to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium-high heat; cook until reduced by half and syrupy, 5–7 minutes. Let sauce cool until thickened slightly, about 10 minutes.

Heat broiler (if broiler is in your oven, place rack in upper third). Season both sides of one 1½–2-lb. skinless or skin-on center-cut salmon fillet with kosher salt. Place, skin side down, in a skillet or baking dish. Transfer one third of sauce to a small bowl and set aside for serving.
Brush about half of remaining sauce over fillet. (If the salmon has a lot of room around it in the pan, line with foil to prevent runoff sauce from burning onto pan.)
Broil salmon until sauce is just starting to burn in spots, 4–7 minutes. Brush remaining sauce over fillet and broil until deeply charred and salmon is opaque all the way through, about 5 minutes.
Remove fish from oven and spoon reserved sauce over. Top with thinly sliced scallions and/or toasted sesame seeds if desired.

items.name: Smashed Beef Koftas with Yogurt Sauce
ingredients: ¼ tsp cayenne pepper , optional (for a bit spicy)
1 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt (halve for table salt, +50% for flakes)
¼ cup walnuts , crumbled into large pieces with your hands – or chopped almonds or pecans
1 large Lebanese cucumber (Persian cucumbers), about 25cm/10" long
3 tbsp finely sliced mint , plus extra for sprinkling (substitute coriander/cilantro, or 2 tsp dried mint in yogurt sauce)
½ tsp cooking salt / kosher salt
1 tbsp pomegranate molasses (balsamic glaze is an excellent substitute – Note 2)
steps: Cucumber Yogurt Sauce – Grate the cucumber into a bowl using a standard box grater. Add yogurt and mint, mix, then leave on the counter while you make the beef.
Smashed beef kofta – Grate the onion into a bowl using the same box grater. Add all the remaining kofta ingredients and mix well using your hands.

Raggedy lumps of meat – Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan over medium high heat. Use your hands to drop chunks of beef into the pan – about 2.5 cm/1" lumps (no need to be accurate), no rolling, just pinch off raggedy lumps. The pan will be full, it's ok, the meat shrinks.

Brown first side 5 – 7 min – Leave undisturbed and cook for 5 to 7 minutes until the underside is dark golden (beef juices might come out because the pan is crowded but then it will evaporate), all the clumps of beef should be cooked through.

Add walnuts and cranberries – Flip the beef as best you can (there's lots of pieces so hard to be accurate, it's fine, just do your best) and leave for 1 minute to get a bit of colour on that side. Add the walnuts and cranberries then gently stir for another 1 minute. Remove from the stove.
Salt – Add the salt into the yogurt sauce and mix.

Serve – Spread the yogurt sauce on a large plate, or in 4 individual bowls. Spoon the beef over, drizzle with pomegranate molasses, olive oil, scatter with mint and serve with warm pita bread on the side.

How to eat – The idea here is to use the pita bread to scoop yogurt and beef straight off the plate, or you can stuff inside pita pockets! You could also make wraps and add tomato, shredded lettuce, and onion, or make rice bowls with basmati rice and chopped tomatoes on the side.

items.name: Italian Wedding Soup
ingredients: ⅛ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
1 lb. ground Italian sausage hot, mild, or sweet,
½ cup small pasta I used pearled couscous, $0.41**
steps: Gather the ingredients for your meatballs. I find making the meatballs first helps this recipe go a bit faster! You can also form your meatballs a day in advance, or freeze them for easier use later on.
Mix dry ingredients for meatballs; combine the breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan cheese, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Stir to combine.
Add the Italian sausage, breadcrumb mixture, and egg to a large bowl.
Use your hands or a fork to mix them together until just combined.
Divide and shape the mixture into 20 small meatballs, about 1 Tbsp each. Set the meatballs aside.
Gather ingredients for the soup.
Dice the onion, carrots, and celery, and mince the garlic.
Add the olive oil to a large soup pot and heat over medium. Add the diced vegetables, garlic, and Italian seasoning, cooking until the vegetables have softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the chicken broth to the soup, stir to combine, then place a lid on top and bring it up to a boil.
Once the soup is boiling, add the meatballs to the soup and continue to boil until the meatballs are cooked through (about 10 minutes).

(Optional) If you prefer browned meatballs, you can cook them in a skillet with a little olive oil first over medium heat until browned on the outside, then transfer to the boiling soup to finish cooking at this stage in the recipe.
Add the tiny pasta to the boiling soup and continue to boil until the pasta is tender (about 6 minutes).
Finally, stir in the fresh spinach until wilted. Give the soup a taste and adjust the seasonings to your liking. Top with optional parsley, if using. Serve hot and enjoy!

items.name: Steak au Poivre (Black Pepper Steak)
ingredients: 4 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, divided
2 tablespoons cognac, brandy, white wine, or a splash of white wine vinegar
½ cup crème fraîche or sour cream
steps: Crush the peppercorns. Using a mortar and pestle, coarsely crack the black peppercorns. Alternatively, fold the whole peppercorns into a parchment paper packet, like an envelope, and bash them with a kitchen mallet. You want mostly broken peppercorns, with some whole pieces and some crumble.
Using a peppermill (even on the coarse setting) is likely finer than what you’re after. Ideally, the pepper will have a more varied texture with bigger pieces.

Pepper the steaks. Pat steaks dry with a paper towel. Season each side of the steak liberally with Kosher salt. Then, evenly sprinkle cracked peppercorns all across one side of each steak. Press with your palms to pack the peppercorns in so they stick.

Sear the steaks. In a heavy-bottomed skillet, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium-high heat. Working in two batches to avoid crowding the pan, place the steaks in the pan, peppercorn-side up, which maximizes the caramelized flavor and reduces the chance of burning the peppercorns.
Sear steaks for about 3 to 4 minutes, undisturbed, per side, flipping with care so the peppercorn crust can stay intact.

Cook until desired level of doneness: For rare, cook until the internal temperature reaches 120°F, for medium-rare aim for 130°F, medium 140°F, medium-well 150°F, and for well-done 160°F. Transfer the steaks to a plate, cover with foil, and set aside.
The steaks will continue to cook and increase in temperature a few more degrees as they rest, so we recommend removing them from the pan at these temperatures.

Make the pan sauce. In the same skillet, add the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil and turn the heat down to medium. Toss in the shallots and sauté until translucent and lightly browned, about 2 minutes. Add the cognac to the pan, scraping up all the bits of fond stuck on the bottom of the pan.
Let the cognac come to a light boil for about 1 minute (for the alcohol to evaporate) before adding in the beef stock, creme fraiche, and sprigs of thyme.

Reduce the sauce: Stir and simmer until the sauce reduces and thickens, About 5 or 6 minutes, or until the sauce coats the back of a wooden spoon. Finally, stir in the Dijon mustard. Taste and season with salt if needed.

Finish and serve. To serve, fish out the thyme sprigs and pour the sauce over your cooked steaks, or serve the sauce on the side. If you like, you can slice the steaks, plate them, and then drizzle the sauce on top.

items.name: Roasted Brussels Sprouts
ingredients: 3 lb. brussels sprouts, trimmed, halved, quartered if large
¼ cup plus 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt
½ tsp. freshly ground black pepper
steps: Preheat oven to 450°. Toss 3 lb. brussels sprouts, trimmed, halved, quartered if large, ¼ cup plus 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and ½ tsp. freshly ground black pepper on a rimmed baking sheet to coat.

Arrange in a single layer and roast, tossing occasionally, until tender and browned, 15–25 minutes. MORE WAYS TO ROAST BRUSSELS SPROUTS: Once you’ve mastered the basics, there are plenty of ways to change things up.

Try frico’ed brussels sprouts with a crispy Parmesan crust; brussels sprouts with warm honey glaze or garlicky balsamic brussels sprouts for a savory-sweet finish; or, for a little heat, make roasted brussels sprouts with gochujang brown butter.

items.name: 7 Day High Protein Diet Meal Plan
Apple Spice Cake
ingredients: 2 Tbsp apple spice mix see above
1 stick unsalted butter browned and cooled,
½ cup neutral oil canola or vegetable,
¼ cup apple juice or cider
2 Granny Smith apples peeled and diced, (about 2 cups) $2.18***
2 Honeycrisp or Fuji apples peeled and diced, (about 2 cups) $3.32***
steps: Gather ingredients for cake and spice mix. Preheat oven to 350℉.
Over medium heat, melt a stick of unsalted butter and keep an eye on it, watching for it to begin browning.
Peel and core apples.

Dice apples into small pieces, about 1-2 cm in size. While you’re preparing the apples, keep an eye on your browning butter, giving it a little swirl in the pan every so often, making sure the butter solids don’t burn.
At the halfway point, your butter will look a bit foamy on top, and the butter solids will start to turn golden yellow.
Combine dry cake ingredients (flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt) and the apple spice mix in a large mixing bowl.

Your butter will be perfectly browned after 5-10 minutes over medium heat. Remove the butter from the heat once it’s golden brown and the foam on top has dissipated. Let it cool for a few minutes, swirling it every now and then to help it cool and keep it from burning from the residual heat.

Combine the wet cake ingredients (eggs, neutral oil, applesauce, apple juice or cider, vanilla extract) and the sugars (brown and granulated white sugar). Add the cooled brown butter and mix to combine.
Little by little, add some of the dry mixture to the wet mixture. With a hand mixer on low, continue to add dry mix and blend until the batter is completely combined.
Then, fold in all of the diced apples.
Spray or butter a 9×13 inch pan.
Pour the apple spice cake mix into the prepared 9×13 pan.
Bake at 350℉ for 45 min or until a toothpick comes out clean when inserted in the center of the cake.
Let the cake completely cool, then top with powdered sugar.

items.name: Cider-Braised Sausage and Lentils
ingredients: 6–8 smoked Austrian or German sausages (1–1½ lb.)
1 large red or yellow onion, finely chopped
3 celery stalks, leaves reserved, finely chopped
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, divided
2 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
1½ cups French green lentils, picked through, rinsed
½ cup finely chopped parsley, plus leaves for serving
3 Tbsp. Dijon or whole grain mustard
1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar or red wine vinegar
steps: Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium heavy pot over medium-high. Cook 6–8 smoked Austrian or German sausages (1–1½ lb.), turning often, until deeply browned on all sides, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a plate.

Combine 1 large red or yellow onion, finely chopped, 3 celery stalks, finely chopped, 1 large carrot, peeled, finely chopped, 1 tsp. freshly ground pepper, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in same pan.

Reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring often and scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan, until vegetables are softened, 6–8 minutes. Add 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and cook, stirring, just until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add 2 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, 1½ cups apple cider, 1½ cups French green lentils, picked through, rinsed, ½ cup finely chopped parsley, 3 Tbsp. Dijon or whole grain mustard, and remaining ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt to pan.

Increase heat to high and bring to a boil. Cook until liquid is slightly reduced, about 5 minutes. Cover pan, reduce heat to medium-low, and cook until lentils are tender and most of the liquid is absorbed but mixture is still saucy, 30–35 minutes.

Uncover pan and stir in 1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar or red wine vinegar. Nestle sausages into lentil mixture and add any juices pooled on plate. Simmer until sausages are warmed through, about 5 minutes. Top with parsley leaves and reserved celery leaves to serve.

items.name: Mille-Feuille
ingredients: 2 sheets frozen butter puff pastry , 25cm / 10" squares (185g/6oz each), just thawed (Note 1)
1 ½ tbsp soft icing sugar / powdered sugar
1 cup full fat milk (low-fat works too)
½ cup thickened cream / heavy cream , or other whipping cream
1 vanilla bean , split lengthways and seeds scraped out, or 1 tsp vanilla bean paste (Note 2)
3 egg yolks from large eggs (50 – 55g/2oz each in shell) – see here for using egg whites
½ cup caster sugar / superfine sugar , substitute regular / granulated white sugar
1 tbsp / 15g unsalted butter , cold, cut into small 0.7cm / ¼" cubes
¾ cup thickened cream / heavy cream , or other whipping cream (not double cream)
3 tbsp water , just cold tap water
1 cup soft icing sugar / powdered sugar , sifted
4 tsp full fat milk (low-fat works too)
2 tbsp dark chocolate chips / US: semi-sweet chips (Note 4)
steps: Bake puff pastry pressed between sheets. Spread with vanilla icing, pipe chocolate lines then use a toothpick to make the Mille Feuille pattern. Make custard the usual way – it is extra thick.

Cool then incorporate gelatine and whipped cream – the whipped cream lightens it and the gelatine makes the Mille Feuille sliceable. Pipe between puff pastry layers, chill 6 hours to properly set before slicing.
Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F (160°C fan-forced).
Cut each pastry sheet in half, you’ll use 3 halves and pop the 4th back in the freezer for another day.

Prick and dust – Turn 2 baking trays upside down and cover with a sheet of baking paper / parchment paper (Note 5). Place one puff pastry sheet on one tray and two on the other, spaced out as much as you can. Prick all over with a fork (about 30 pricks on each piece). Dust all over with icing sugar using a sifter.
Weigh down – Cover each pastry with another sheet of baking paper / parchment paper and place another tray on top to keep them from puffing up as they bake.

Bake 30 minutes, swapping and turning the trays halfway through, until deep golden and crisp. (The one with 2 sheets on it might take a few extra minutes). Place them on a wire rack and cool completely.
Trim each puff pastry sheets to make them all the same size using a sharp serrated knife. You can either use a ruler or stack them, using one as the master template.

Infuse milk – Put the milk, cream, vanilla bean seeds and used vanilla bean into a large saucepan (~20 cm/8" wide). Heat over medium heat until just below boiling. Remove from heat, cover, and let sit 10 minutes to steep.

Whisk yolks – In a medium size bowl, whisk egg yolks and sugar. It will become like wet sand at first, then will turn liquidy and smooth. Add cornflour and flour, whisk until smooth – it will be like a thick cake batter.
Remove vanilla bean from the milk and use your fingers to squeeze all the milk out into the saucepan. Discard used bean.
Temper eggs – While whisking constantly, slowly pour half the vanilla milk mixture into the yolk bowl. Once combined, pour the mixture into the saucepan with the remaining milk and whisk to combine.
Thicken custard – Return the saucepan on medium heat (or medium low if you have a strong burner).

Whisk constantly – leisurely at first, then more briskly as the mixture starts to heat up at which point it will start to thicken into a thick custard – around 7 to 10 minutes, even longer if using a very low heat to be safe.
If you see lumps like scrambled eggs, move it off the heat straight away and whisk them out vigorously until smooth then return to the stove.

Custard goal thickness – The custard is ready when it is very thick dolloping consistency (see video at 2.20 minutes). You should be able to draw a path across the base of the pan and the pan base stays visible. This custard is thicker than usual so you cannot rely on the "bubble" test.

Finish – Remove from the stove. Whisk in the cold butter cubes until incorporated (the butter must be cold, not room temperature else custard may split). Immediately pour into a large bowl, smooth surface, then cover with cling wrap touching the surface to prevent a skin from forming.
Cool on the counter for 30 minutes, then refrigerate for 45 minutes or until it is cool and firms up to a soft rubber-like consistency. (You can even leave it overnight).
Vanilla icing – In a small bowl, whisk icing sugar, vanilla, and milk until smooth. (Don't make this ahead as it will crust over).

Melted chocolate – Place the chocolate chips in a microwave-safe bowl and melt over (3 × 20-second microwave bursts), stirring between each. Transfer to a small piping bag or zip-lock bag. Snip a 2 mm hole (1/6"). (Only melt chocolate just prior to using to ensure it remains fluid).

Mille Feuille icing pattern (see video at 3.58 minutes and step photos) – Place one piece of puff pastry on a rack set on a tray (to catch drips). Spread evenly with the vanilla icing. Pipe on thin lines of the chocolate icing lengthways, making the lines 1 cm / 0.4" apart.
Working quickly before the chocolate sets, use a toothpick to drag through the lines (1.5 cm / 0.6" apart), alternating one way and then the other, to make the classic mille-feuille pattern.
Fridge 30 minutes – Place in the fridge for at least 30 minutes to let it set. It can stay for longer, until you're ready to assemble.

Bloom gelatine – Place the cold water in a small heatproof bowl and sprinkle the gelatine evenly over the surface. Whisk to combine, then leave for 3 minutes until firm and rubbery (this is called "blooming"). Microwave for 15 seconds until melted (do not boil), then cool for 5 minutes.

Loosen custard – Remove the chilled custard from the fridge, it will have firmed up into a soft rubber. Then use a rubber spatula to soften the custard as best you can, I just sort of smear it. It won't become soft creamy, it will be like a soft mushy paste.

Combine custard and gelatine – Transfer a ¼ of the custard into a large saucepan (~20 cm/8" wide) and warm it over low heat, whisking, until it softens a bit more. It won't become fluid but it will be a very soft paste.

Still on the stove, add gelatine and whisk until smooth, it will be like a thick batter consistency. Whisk in another ¼ of the custard until smooth, then remove from the stove and pour that mixture into the custard bowl. Whisk vigorously until smooth.
Set aside to cool slightly while you whip the cream.

Whisk in whipped cream – Beat the cream using an electric beater or stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment until stiff peaks form (upright peaks). Put a quarter of the cream into the custard, then beat it in with the electric beater. Add remaining cream then beat again until smooth. Congratulations, you've made diplomate cream!

Fridge 20 min only – Cover the bowl and refrigerate for 20 minutes so it firms up enough to pipe, but still creamy enough to scoop. Do not refrigerate longer else the gelatine will make the custard set. If you accidentally do this, gently warm to soften then refrigerate again.

Beat smooth – Remove the diplomate cream from the fridge. It will be like a block of soft rubber. Using an electric beater, beat on high for 30 seconds or until the custard is loosened and smooth. Transfer half the custard into a large piping bag and snip the tip of the bag so you have a 1cm / 0.4" round hole (or use a round nozzle).

Layer 1 – Place one cooked pastry sheet on a cutting board. Pipe lengthways on the pastry sheet – I do 6 rows – to cover all the pastry with diplomate cream, aiming to use all the diplomate cream. Dip an offset spatula in warm water then gently smooth the top.
Layer 2 – Place the second pastry sheet on top, press lightly. Fill the piping bag with the remaining diplomate cream and repeat the piping. Smooth the top again.
Layer 3 – Gently place the iced pastry on top, icing facing up. Use any leftover diplomate cream to pipe along the short edges to fill any gaps in the custard and use the offset spatula to smooth it.
Chill – Refrigerate at least 6 hours to set (I usually refrigerate overnight, to be sure).
Slice – Use a sharp serrated knife to cut into 6 pieces, wiping the blade between each slice. If you can, wait another 30 minutes before eating as the custard is even nicer if it's not fridge-cold!

items.name: Chicken Curry
ingredients: 1 large potato (russet or yukon gold, peeled and diced small (8 ounces))
steps: Heat oil in a large deep skillet, over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and sauté 1 minute. Add cumin, masala and curry powder and mix well, cooking 1 minute.
Place chicken in the pan and season with 1 teaspoon salt.
Add tomatoes, cilantro, coconut milk and water.
Stir all ingredients and cover pan, simmer on medium-low until chicken is cooked through, about 30 minutes.
Add potatoes, ½ teaspoon salt and simmer, covered an additional 10 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender. Taste for salt and adjust, as needed.
Reduce water to ½ cup and cook the chicken after step 4 on high pressure for 15 minutes, quick release then add potatoes, high pressure 5 minutes. Let it release naturally.

items.name: Creamy Miso Mushroom Pasta
ingredients: 12 oz. egg-based pasta (such as fettuccine nests)
½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
1 lb. crimini or mixed mushrooms (such as button, maitake, oyster, and/or shiitake), sliced ¼" thick or torn into bite-size pieces
4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into pieces
1 oz. Parmesan, finely grated (about ½ cup), plus more for serving
steps: Cook 12 oz. egg-based pasta (such as fettuccine nests) in a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring occasionally, until al dente, about 1 minute less than package directions.

Meanwhile, heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over high. Add 1 lb. crimini or mixed mushrooms (such as button, maitake, oyster, and/or shiitake), sliced ¼" thick or torn into bite-size pieces, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt and toss to coat evenly.
Spread out into an even layer and cook, undisturbed, until mushrooms are starting to release their liquid, 2–3 minutes (do not be alarmed; there will be a lot).
Continue to cook, tossing occasionally, until moisture is almost completely evaporated and edges of mushrooms are starting to brown, 6–8 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium-high; add 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Cook, tossing often, until garlic is fragrant and golden, 1–2 minutes.

Pour in ¾ cup dry white wine, scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan with a sturdy spatula or flat-edged wooden spoon, and cook until wine is mostly evaporated (you should have about 1 Tbsp. liquid left in pan), about 4 minutes. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add 4 Tbsp.

unsalted butter, cut into pieces, and 2 Tbsp. white miso and stir until melted and combined. Slowly pour in ½ cup heavy cream, scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan; simmer until thickened slightly, 2–3 minutes. Add 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce; season with freshly ground pepper.
Taste and add more salt if needed.

Using tongs, transfer pasta to mushroom mixture and add 1 cup pasta cooking liquid. Increase heat to medium and bring to a simmer. Cook, tossing constantly and adding ½–1 cup more pasta cooking liquid to reach desired sauce consistency if needed, until pasta is al dente and liquid has thickened slightly, about 3 minutes.
Remove pan from heat. Add 1 oz. Parmesan, finely grated (about ½ cup) to pasta and toss to combine. Season generously with more pepper; taste and season with more salt if needed.
Divide pasta among shallow bowls and top with more Parmesan and pepper.

items.name: Pumpkin Cornbread Muffins
ingredients: ¾ cup low-fat milk (or dairy-free milk)
⅔ cup maple syrup (I used sugar-free Wholesome Yum)
2 tablespoons unsalted butter (melted and cooled (plus more for serving if desired))
1 cup all purpose flour (or gluten-free flour mix)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400° F and spray a 12-cup muffin tin generously with nonstick cooking spray.
Add the pumpkin, milk, maple syrup, eggs, and butter to a medium mixing bowl. Whisk to combine and set aside.
To a large mixing bowl, add the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, salt, pumpkin spice (if using) and cinnamon. Whisk to combine.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix until just combined and no streaks of flour remain. Be careful not to over mix.
Spoon the batter into the prepared muffin tin, dividing the batter equally between the cups.

Bake for 15 to 16 minutes, until a toothpick inserted into the center of the muffins comes out clean. Remove from the oven and let cool in the muffin tin for 10 minutes. Remove from the muffin tin and serve warm. Serve with extra butter, if desired.

items.name: Baked Chicken Breast Recipe
ingredients: 4 chicken breasts boneless, skinless (approx. 8 oz each) $7.14*
1 Tbsp granulated sugar optional, (can omit for keto/low-carb) $0.02**
2 tsp smoked paprika or sweet paprika,
½ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
½ tsp brown sugar optional (omit for sugar-free/keto) $0.01**
steps: Gather ingredients.

Place the chicken breasts between sheets of plastic wrap or put them inside a gallon-size baggie. Use a meat mallet or rolling pin to pound the thicker ends until each breast is an even ½- to ¾-inch thickness throughout.
In a large bowl, add the pounded chicken, 2 quarts of cold water, 2 Tbsp kosher salt, and 1 Tbsp granulated sugar. You can also brine the chicken breasts in a Gallon size (maybe 2) zip-top bag.
Cover and refrigerate the submerged chicken breasts in the brine for 30 minutes. Do not exceed 45 minutes to prevent the meat texture from breaking down.
Preheat your oven to 425°F. In a small bowl, combine the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, and brown sugar (if using).

Remove chicken from the brine, rinse quickly under cold water, and thoroughly pat completely dry with clean paper towels.*** Drizzle the breasts with olive oil, then rub the spice mix evenly over all sides of the chicken.

Arrange seasoned chicken breasts in a single layer in a 9×13-inch baking dish or rimmed baking sheet. Bake uncovered at 425°F for 18-20 minutes, or until an instant-read thermometer registers 160-165°F in the thickest part of each chicken breast.

Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate, loosely tent with aluminum foil, and let rest for 5-10 minutes before cutting. The residual heat will finish bringing the internal temperature to 165°F while locking in all the juices. (see notes)

items.name: BA’s Best Chocolate Chip Cookies
ingredients: 1½ cups plus 1 Tbsp. (200 g) all-purpose flour (spooning into measuring cups, then leveling)
1¼ tsp. (4 g) Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. (4 g) Morton kosher salt
¾ cup (1½ sticks; 169 g) unsalted butter, divided
6 oz. (170 g) bittersweet chocolate (60%–70% cacao), coarsely chopped, or semisweet chocolate chips
steps: Place racks in upper and lower thirds of oven; preheat to 375°. Whisk 1½ cups plus 1 Tbsp. (200 g) all-purpose flour, 1¼ tsp. (4 g) Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. (4 g) Morton kosher salt, and ¾ tsp. (4 g) baking soda in a small bowl; set flour mixture aside.

Cook ½ cup (1 stick; 113 g) unsalted butter in a large saucepan over medium heat, swirling often and scraping bottom of pan with a heatproof rubber spatula, until butter foams, then browns, about 4 minutes.

Scrape melted butter and any brown bits to a large heatproof mixing bowl and let cool 1 minute. Cut remaining ¼ cup (½ stick; 56 g) unsalted butter into small pieces and add to brown butter (it should start to melt but not foam and sizzle, so test with one piece before adding the rest).

Once butter is melted, add 1 cup (200 g) (packed) dark brown sugar and ¼ cup (50 g) granulated sugar and whisk, breaking up any clumps, until sugar is incorporated and no lumps remain. Add 1 large egg and 2 large egg yolks and whisk until sugar dissolves and mixture is smooth, about 30 seconds.
Whisk in 2 tsp. vanilla extract. Using rubber spatula, fold reserved dry ingredients into butter mixture just until no dry spots remain, then fold in 6 oz.

(170 g) bittersweet chocolate (60%–70% cacao), coarsely chopped, or semisweet chocolate chips (the cookie dough will be soft but should hold its shape once scooped; if it slumps or oozes after being scooped, stir dough back together several times and let rest 5–10 minutes until scoops hold their shape as the flour hydrates).

Using a 1½-oz. scoop (3 Tbsp.), portion out 16 balls of dough and divide between 2 parchment-paper-lined rimmed baking sheets. Bake cookies, rotating sheets if cookies are browning very unevenly (otherwise, just leave them alone), until deep golden brown and firm around the edges, 8–10 minutes.

Let cool on baking sheets. Do Ahead: Dough balls can be portioned 3 months ahead; freeze on cookie sheets and then transfer to a resealable plastic bag. Bake from frozen, adding 1–2 minutes onto the cook time. Cookies can be baked 3 days ahead. Store in an airtight container at room temperature.
